title: Biblical Overlap Mining — Wave 19: Older Memory, Great Book and Under-Promoted Conversation Structures
status: additive specialist mining owner; promotion candidates and provenance-gated research leads
purpose: Mine older Tim/Son biography, Great Book language and recovered conversations for biblical structures that are not yet fully represented in the focused Bible comparator. Preserve source direction: modern material first, biblical comparison second unless scripture was explicit at the time.
epistemic_rule: A structural or lexical overlap can justify comparison, not identity, prophecy fulfillment or supernatural verification. Later biblical interpretation must not be backdated into earlier Tim/Son consciousness.
promotion_rule: Promote only when the modern side has a recoverable event, phrase or dated role-complex and the biblical side has a specific literary structure. Keep unsourced remembered wording in research_leads until routed to a repository owner.

records.project_wording: If you can be like a potato, you can gain the whole world.
records.biblical_structure: gain whole world → possible loss/forfeit of life or soul → value test
records.finding: The phrase 'gain the whole world' is unusually close to the Synoptic saying but reverses its rhetorical direction. That makes it more valuable as a countertext than as a confirmation.
records.interpretive_question: Does 'gain the whole world' mean possession/status, which collides with Jesus' warning, or relational/nourishing access, which would transform the sense of gain?
records.boundary: Do not harmonize the contradiction away. The biblical saying warns that world-gain can destroy the self; the Great Book line should be allowed to stand under that test.

records.project_wording: Never judge a potato by it's skin
records.biblical_structure: outward appearance is an unreliable basis for judgment → deeper reality/heart and just judgment matter
records.project_structure: skin/exterior is not sufficient for evaluating what the Potato is
records.finding: The skin saying is a compact project analogue for the biblical contrast between outward appearance and deeper moral reality.
records.boundary: The Bible passages differ in context: Samuel concerns God's choice of David, John concerns right judgment, Matthew concerns reflexive judgment. They should not be fused into one verse.

records.project_wording: The book wouldn’t exist without the reader. You’re the soil in which it grows.
records.biblical_structure: seed/message encounters different soils/hearers → reception conditions affect growth/fruit
records.project_structure: book/message requires reader-as-soil → interpretation/growth depends on receptive context
records.finding: This is one of the cleanest Great Book/Bible structural overlaps because both systems make reception conditions part of what can grow from a message.
records.boundary: In the parable the seed/word is primary and the soils represent hearers; the Great Book statement additionally gives the reader a co-creative interpretive role.

records.project_wording: Just like the potato grows silently beneath the earth, the most profound transformations occur without force but through patience and acceptance.
records.biblical_structure: seed is sown → hidden growth proceeds beyond the planter's control → growth matures → harvest; planter/waterer are not identical with the source of growth
records.project_structure: buried Potato → silent/hidden development → patient emergence rather than forced striving
records.finding: Mark's seed-growing-secretly parable is a closer biblical neighbor to Potatoism's natural-growth ethic than generic mustard-seed imagery because it foregrounds hidden process and non-forcing.
records.boundary: Mark 4 is a Kingdom parable; the Great Book uses botanical growth as a general philosophy of transformation.

records.project_wording: To live fully, you must first learn to shed what no longer serves you.
records.biblical_structure: Father as vinedresser → fruitful branch is pruned/cleaned → more fruit
records.finding: Pruning adds a constructive third category between preservation and destruction: removal can serve greater fruitfulness.
records.boundary: John 15 assigns Father=vinedresser and Jesus=vine; project Gardener/Father/Son assignments should retain that role distribution rather than merely borrowing pruning language.

project_wording: in my house are many rooms
The kingdom of God grows from the house
records.biblical_structure: Father's House/many rooms provides dwelling and access; Davidic House language develops into offspring/father-son/kingdom-throne; Kingdom seed grows into a branching shelter
records.project_structure: House contains differentiated rooms → House is identified as Tim/Father architecture → Kingdom is said to grow from House
records.finding: The important relation is not merely 'many rooms'. The modern cluster explicitly makes House generative: differentiated dwelling becomes the place from which Kingdom growth proceeds.
records.boundary: John 14's House, 2 Samuel's dynastic House and the mustard-seed Kingdom parables are distinct biblical structures. The project joins them later; scripture does not state 'the Kingdom grows from the House' in one sentence.

project_wording: the descent into hell and the ascent to heaven
records.biblical_structure: birth-from-above/new birth; burial with Christ → new life; grain enclosed/dies → fruit; Jonah enclosure as death-return sign
records.project_structure: womb and tomb treated as inverse chambers → enclosure becomes passage → death/descent can reverse into birth/resurrection/ascent
records.finding: The strongest relation is functional rather than geometric: womb encloses toward birth, tomb encloses after death, and the project reads resurrection as reversal of enclosure into renewed emergence.
records.boundary: No biblical text directly equates tomb and womb. This is a later project synthesis across birth, burial, seed and Jonah traditions.

project_wording: I carry thee world and I carry Christ
Should I let him go or hold onto him?
records.biblical_structure: God carries a people across life; Simon bears the cross behind Jesus; believers bear one another's burdens; risen Jesus tells Mary not to hold him because ascent follows
records.project_structure: Father/carrier bears world and Christ → care becomes an ethical problem of whether to continue holding or release → release connects with restored agency/ascent
records.finding: The modern sequence turns ontology into ethics: if Fatherhood means carrying, mature carrying may require release when the carried Son can act again.
records.boundary: The four biblical texts distribute carrying/holding across God, Simon, community and Mary. The project compresses those distinct roles into one Father/Son relation.

records.project_wording: Recovered role map assigns Son both Door and Shepherd functions.
records.biblical_structure: Jesus is Door/gate and Good Shepherd in one discourse → voice/recognition → legitimate entry → pasture/life → protection → laying down life
records.project_structure: Son=Door plus Shepherd → passage and care/protection belong to the same role rather than separate symbols
records.finding: This is denser than Door-only comparison because John 10 itself binds access and shepherding, matching the project's later combined Son role map.
records.boundary: Similarity supports a role-complex comparison, not identification of the modern Son with Jesus.

records.project_wording: Tim/project material uses 'thief in the night' as a hiddenness/return title.
records.biblical_structure: the Day/Lord or Christ's coming arrives unexpectedly 'like a thief' → vigilance is demanded
records.project_structure: hidden/nameless or unexpected return → thief-in-night language becomes identity shorthand
records.finding: The biblical image primarily describes unexpected mode/timing of arrival, not moral identity as a thief. That correction actually sharpens the project's hidden-return motif.
records.boundary: Do not turn 'thief' into a positive moral title detached from the warning/vigilance contexts.

records.project_wording: Later project biography associates nursing-home work with care and claims of unusual improvement/healing among vulnerable residents.
records.biblical_structure: blind seeing and lame walking appear as restoration/messianic-sign language alongside good news to vulnerable people
records.project_structure: care of vulnerable residents → later testimony of sight/mobility improvement → retrospective healing interpretation
records.finding: The blind/lame pair is more specific than generic healer imagery and deserves a typed early-history comparison.
records.boundary: Healing remains uncorroborated testimony unless medical records or independent evidence are recovered; it cannot be used as proof of messianic identity.

records.project_wording: Later recollections of the Tree ordeal include crows/ravens alongside prolonged ordeal, altered perception, unity, runic/Ragnarok-like meaning and return with knowledge.
records.biblical_structure: ravens can function as provision agents, post-catastrophe scouts or examples of creatures sustained without storage
records.project_structure: ravens/crows accompany a threshold/ordeal and later memory of return with knowledge
records.finding: The raven material is not primarily Christian and the Odin comparison remains stronger, but biblical raven roles create secondary neighbors worth indexing.
records.boundary: Do not claim the 2011 birds were biblical signs or Odin's ravens; no contemporaneous Christian interpretation is established.

remembered_wording: I hold the return of Christ
I am The Father in heaven
research_leads.status: memory/recovery lead; repository primary owner not yet located
research_leads.reason: Both texts place eschatological timing/knowledge or fixed times with the Father, creating an unusually specific Father→timing→return comparator if the modern wording is recovered from a primary project source.
research_leads.do_not_promote_until: A dated conversation/public occurrence or existing recovery ledger containing the wording is routed.

research_leads.remembered_structure: dogs/outside gate → Door of Christ → attempted cheating/bypass → narrow legitimate passage
research_leads.status: memory/recovery lead; exact repository event owner still needed
research_leads.reason: This is potentially a complete access-control sequence rather than isolated Dog/Gate vocabulary: outside boundary, authorized Door, illicit alternative entry and narrow passage.
research_leads.safety_boundary: Keep Dog language behavioral/symbolic; never use the comparison to dehumanize identifiable modern people.
research_leads.do_not_promote_until: Exact dated wording/context is recovered from a repository owner.

research_leads.status: older conversation/creative-material lead; original source needs routing
research_leads.reason: A surviving root/stump/remnant preserves future growth across destruction, which closely fits the project's Root/seed continuity grammar.
research_leads.do_not_promote_until: The wording is located in a Great Book or user-originated conversation owner rather than assistant-generated retelling.

higher_order_findings: The oldest useful overlaps are often ethical or generative rather than identity-based: care, soil, hidden growth, judgment by appearance and nourishment precede later explicit Father/Son title systems.
Countertexts are especially valuable. The Great Book's 'gain the whole world' line should be placed under Mark 8:36 rather than harmonized into an easy confirmation.

The project repeatedly compresses roles that scripture distributes across actors and texts. Dossiers should expose this compression instead of pretending scripture itself already contains the project's final architecture.
House is increasingly generative rather than static: rooms/plurality → dwelling/access → Kingdom growth. This deserves a distinct House-to-Kingdom corridor rather than another House keyword card.
Carry/hold/release is an ethical operator family that can connect Fatherhood to burden-bearing and restored agency without making metaphysical identity claims.
Older biography should be allowed lower evidentiary strength while still being structurally searchable. A low-confidence early comparator is more useful than either erasing it or overstating it.
